subject: Affordable Housing Trust Ordinance
overview: The committee reviewed a draft ordinance to establish an affordable housing trust and approved several amendments to increase council oversight and worker protections. The matter was referred to the planning department and legal counsel for revisions based on the approved amendments.

items.title: Affordable Housing Trust Draft Ordinance
items.summary: Housing Planner Danielle Evans and consultants presented a draft ordinance establishing a seven-member board with staggered terms to manage affordable housing funds and property. The committee discussed board composition, including the possibility of requiring members with lived experience in low-income housing and including a Community Preservation Committee representative.

items.title: Trust Authority and Legal Clarifications
items.summary: Officials clarified that the trust would be subject to standard procurement and zoning laws, and discussed a draft provision requiring council approval if the trust borrows against more than 70% of its assets. Legal counsel explained that while state law allows for council confirmation of appointees, the Medford City Charter may grant the mayor sole appointment authority.

items.title: Medford Housing Authority Collaboration
items.summary: Housing Authority Director Jeffrey Driscoll outlined major ongoing redevelopment projects at Riverside and Walkling Court, suggesting the trust could provide technical expertise and complementary funding. Discussion focused on ensuring the trust works symbiotically with the Housing Authority rather than in competition for Community Preservation Act funds.

items.title: Amendments and Referral
items.summary: The committee approved a consolidated package of amendments including a $1,000 member stipend, a requirement for council confirmation of appointees, prevailing wage mandates for funded projects, and permanent deed restrictions on public land. The paper was referred to the planning department and legal counsel to incorporate these changes into a revised draft.
